questions.stem: CASELET: A company has 1,200 employees in total. 40 % are women. 30 % of the men and 25 % of the women are married. Q: How many UNMARRIED employees does the company have?
questions.explanation: Women = 40 % × 1200 = 480. Men = 720. Married men = 30 % × 720 = 216. Married women = 25 % × 480 = 120. Total married = 336. Unmarried = 1200 − 336 = 864. Multi-step caselet item typical of Bank PO mains.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): Using the figures above, what is the ratio of unmarried men to unmarried women?
questions.explanation: Unmarried men = 720 − 216 = 504. Unmarried women = 480 − 120 = 360. Ratio 504 : 360 = 21 : 15 (divide both by 24).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET: In a school, the ratio of boys to girls is 7 : 5. 60 % of the boys and 40 % of the girls play a sport. If 180 girls DO NOT play a sport, find the total number of students.
questions.explanation: Girls not playing = 60 % of girls = 180 → girls total = 300. Ratio 7:5 → boys = 300 × 7/5 = 420. Total = 720.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): In the same school, how many students in total play a sport?
questions.explanation: Boys playing = 60 % × 420 = 252. Girls playing = 40 % × 300 = 120. Total = 372. Independent second question that forces the student to re-use the caselet numbers.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET: Three candidates A, B, C stood in an election. A got 35 % of the valid votes and B got 45 %. The remainder went to C. If C received 3,600 votes, total valid votes were:
questions.explanation: A + B = 80 % → C = 20 % of valid = 3600 → valid = 18,000. If the question had asked for TOTAL votes (including invalid), an extra step would be needed; as stated it is valid-only.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET: A bank branch disbursed loans to 480 customers last month. 60% of the customers took personal loans (average amount ₹2.5 lakh each) and the remaining took home loans (average amount ₹18 lakh each). How many customers of the branch took home loans?

options.option_text: 144 customers out of 480 took home loans
192 customers out of 480 took home loans
216 customers out of 480 took home loans
288 customers out of 480 took home loans

questions.explanation: Personal loan customers = 60% of 480 = 288; Home loan customers = 480 − 288 = 192. Option A (144) is the trap — it applies 30% instead of 40%, confusing the complement of 60% with 70%.

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): Using the same bank branch data above, what is the ratio of the total amount disbursed as personal loans to the total amount disbursed as home loans?

options.option_text: Personal to home loan disbursed ratio is 5 : 24
Personal to home loan disbursed ratio is 3 : 2
Personal to home loan disbursed ratio is 5 : 36
Personal to home loan disbursed ratio is 2 : 9

questions.explanation: Total personal = 288 × 2.5 = 720 lakh; Total home = 192 × 18 = 3,456 lakh; Ratio = 720 : 3,456 = 5 : 24. Option C (5:36) is the classic trap — it compares only average loan amounts (2.5 : 18) ignoring customer counts. Option B (3:2) uses just the customer-count ratio without applying loan sizes.

questions.stem: CASELET: A public-sector bank reports total advances of ₹60,000 crore and a Gross NPA ratio of 8%. The Gross NPA is distributed across sectors as: Agriculture — 40%, MSME — 35%, and Other sectors — the remainder. What is the Gross NPA of the bank (in ₹ crore)?

options.option_text: Gross NPA of the bank stands at ₹3,600 crore
Gross NPA of the bank stands at ₹4,200 crore
Gross NPA of the bank stands at ₹4,800 crore
Gross NPA of the bank stands at ₹5,400 crore

questions.explanation: Gross NPA = 8% of ₹60,000 crore = ₹4,800 crore. Option A (₹3,600 crore) corresponds to 6% — a common error from confusing Net NPA ratio with Gross NPA ratio. Option B (₹4,200 crore) reflects 7%, another typical misread.

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): Using the same bank's NPA data above, by how much (in ₹ crore) does the Agriculture sector NPA exceed the MSME sector NPA?

options.option_text: Agriculture NPA exceeds MSME NPA by ₹120 crore
Agriculture NPA exceeds MSME NPA by ₹240 crore
Agriculture NPA exceeds MSME NPA by ₹360 crore
Agriculture NPA exceeds MSME NPA by ₹480 crore

questions.explanation: Agriculture NPA = 40% of 4,800 = ₹1,920 crore; MSME NPA = 35% of 4,800 = ₹1,680 crore; Difference = ₹240 crore. Option A (₹120 crore) is the trap — it applies the 5% sector-share gap directly to ₹2,400 (half the NPA) instead of the full ₹4,800 crore base.

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): From the same bank's NPA data, if the bank recovers 25% of the Agriculture NPA and 40% of the MSME NPA during the year, what is the total amount recovered (in ₹ crore) from these two sectors combined?

options.option_text: Total recovery from the two sectors is ₹900 crore
Total recovery from the two sectors is ₹1,050 crore
Total recovery from the two sectors is ₹1,152 crore
Total recovery from the two sectors is ₹1,440 crore

questions.explanation: Agriculture recovery = 25% of ₹1,920 = ₹480 crore; MSME recovery = 40% of ₹1,680 = ₹672 crore; Total = ₹1,152 crore. Option A (₹900 crore) is the trap — it applies the same 25% to the combined Agriculture + MSME NPA of ₹3,600 crore, ignoring differentiated rates. Option D (₹1,440 crore) applies 40% uniformly to both.

questions.stem: CASELET: A cooperative society has 500 members — 60% from urban areas and the rest rural. Among urban members, 2/3 are salaried and the remainder are self-employed (SE). Among rural members, exactly half are salaried and the rest SE. The society lends ₹60,000 to each salaried member at 10% p.a. simple interest, and ₹40,000 to each SE member at 15% p.a. simple interest. What is the total annual interest income (in ₹) earned from all members?

options.option_text: Total annual interest from all members is ₹24,00,000
Total annual interest from all members is ₹26,00,000
Total annual interest from all members is ₹30,00,000
Total annual interest from all members is ₹36,00,000

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): Using the same cooperative society data, the total loan disbursed to urban salaried members is what fraction of the total loan disbursed to all 500 members?

options.option_text: Urban salaried share of total loan disbursed is 2/5
Urban salaried share of total loan disbursed is 8/13
Urban salaried share of total loan disbursed is 6/13
Urban salaried share of total loan disbursed is 3/13

questions.explanation: Urban salaried loan = 200 × ₹60,000 = ₹1,20,00,000; Total loan = 1,20,00,000 + 40,00,000 + 60,00,000 + 40,00,000 = ₹2,60,00,000; Fraction = 120/260 = 6/13. Option B (8/13) is the most dangerous trap — it computes total urban loan (₹1,60,00,000) as a share of ₹2,60,00,000, conflating all urban members with urban salaried alone. Option A (2/5) merely uses the member count ratio 200/500 without applying loan amounts.
